author: rsi_demo
title: G4 · 接受
body:
Generation 4 lifts the two best remaining levers. matMul gains a 1×4 j-tile on top of gen 3's already-transposed i-j-k loop, so a[i,k..k+7] is loaded once and feeds 32 independent FMAs across four c[i,j] accumulators that live in registers — a-load traffic drops 4× and V8's OoO pipeline gets far more work to overlap, projected to push matMul from 1.82× to ≈ 2.3-2.7× on holdout. primesUpTo swaps the gen-3 byte-packed odd sieve for a bit-packed odd sieve (8× smaller, 31 KB for n=500000, fully L1-resident instead of spilling 250 KB to L2); the RMW-per-mark overhead is overwhelmed by the L1 hit, projected to push primesUpTo from 25.8× to ≈ 35-65×. Even on the pessimistic end (matMul 2.0, primes 30) the combined geomean multiplier is ≈ 1.03, taking 28.27× to ≈ 29.3×; realistically we expect 30-32×, comfortably clearing the 29.69× gate. All edge cases (empty inputs, n=0/1/2 matrices, bit/byte index math, multiple-of-4 alignment) were traced by hand; the six unchanged exports remain identical to gen 3.
